title: DevLoop: Lightweight Onramp Playbook (Draft)
summary: Working draft for a minimal, reproducible SDK onramp focused on the local developer loop. Goal: get an engineer from zero to a validated mock-and-smoke flow in ~45 minutes using a CLI-first path.
body:
Purpose:
- Create a tiny, opinionated onramp that prioritizes speed-to-feedback. Not a full course; a single developer path that proves core DX assumptions.
- Emphasize: CLI-first, local mock server, 1 sample app (chat + embeddings), telemetry contract, and smoke tests.

Audience:
- New devs evaluating Redwood SDKs (backend/frontend engineers, platform engineers).
- Internal demos for sales/solutions when wanting a live developer loop.

Success metrics (how we measure onramp health):
- Time-to-first-successful-generate (target < 45 minutes)
- % of users who run smoke tests after install (target > 60%)
- Number of issues filed against starter in first week (signal friction)
- Qualitative NPS from 1:1 onboarding sessions

Core flow (happy path) - steps for the README and CLI guide:
1) Prereqs: Node 18+/Python 3.10+, Docker optional.
2) Clone starter repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/devloop-starter.git
3) Install local dev tool: npm i -g @redwood/infer-cli (or pipx install redwood-infer)
4) Start local mock server: redwood infer mock --port 8080 --model small --seed-data examples/chat-examples.json
5) Run sample app: cd sample-app && yarn dev (env: REDWOOD_HOST=http://localhost:8080)
6) Trigger smoke: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize this repo in one sentence."}'
7) Validate telemetry: redwood infer diag tail --since 1m (should show request_id, model_variant, latency_ms)

What the mock server must cover (minimum):
- /generate (sync + stream toggle)
- /chat (session id passthrough + KV cache hint header)
- /embeddings (deterministic output for example inputs)
- healthz and /metrics (basic prometheus counters)

Scaffolded artifacts in repo:
- sample-app/ (express + small fronted single page) with 2 flows: chat UI and document search with embeddings\- quick-checks/ (smoke test scripts)
- infra-local/ (docker-compose for optional local Redis for cache+kv)
- telemetry/contract.md (list of required fields: request_id, sdk_version, model_id, client_latency_ms)
- prompts/ (opinionated prompt templates for the sample app)

Developer checklist (for maintainers shipping the starter):
- [ ] Reduce install surface: single command for both CLI + deps (script: bootstrap.sh)
- [ ] Add an "easy mode" that runs everything via Docker for non-node users
- [ ] Include offline fallback data (small embedding index) so demo still works without network
- [ ] Provide clear rollback steps if mock server fails (how to revert local changes)

Telemetry contract (brief):
- Required keys in all SDK calls emitted to diag stream: request_id, timestamp_iso, client_id (anon ok), sdk_lang, sdk_version, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms
- Use this to drive two UI checks in Console: "first-success" funnel and latency distribution

Failure modes to call out (and quick fixes):
- Docker port collision: provide fallback ports and automatic prompts to user
- Missing API key: dev CLI should surface the minimal env var name and a one-click copy command to set a local .env
- Streaming hang: mock server should send final sentinel and allow client to time out after 8s by default

Testing & gating for PRs (owners):
- CI must run smoke scripts against a test instance of mock server
- Linting: typescript + prettier + simple security scan on deps
- UX: recorded video (30s max) showing the entire happy path for release changes

Open questions / items for product review:
- Do we keep both Node and Python starter apps? (tradeoffs: maintenance vs audience breadth)
- How aggressively do we document latency expectations (numbers per model) in starter?
- Should the default mock model be a quantized open checkpoint or a locally deterministic stub?

Publishing plan (MVP -> GA):
- MVP (iter 0): single Node sample-app + mock server + README + smoke tests. Internal only.
- Iter 1: add Python sample, Docker easy-mode, short video walkthrough; invite 10 external partners for feedback.
- GA: publish in templates marketplace, add one-click GitHub template, landing page with quick metrics.

Notes to self / quick reminders (informal):
- Keep text minimal on README, link to longer docs in Console docs space.
- Example prompts should avoid PII and be short (< 80 tokens).
- Reuse existing telemetry fields from "diag" stream to avoid extra migration work.

Quick commands appendix (copyable):
- Clone + bootstrap: git clone .../devloop-starter && cd devloop-starter && ./bootstrap.sh
- Start mock (node): npm run mock:start
- Run smoke locally: ./quick-checks/run-all.sh
- Tail telemetry: redwood infer diag tail --filter sample-app

Draft timeline (2-week sprint idea):
- Week 1: build Node sample + basic mock + README + smoke tests
- Week 2: Docker mode, telemetry contract review, small polish, internal trial

References and related internal pages (docs + tickets):
- Confluence: DEV-ONRAMP home (linked above)
- Ticket: JIRA-ONRAMP-42 (starter repo + infra)
- PR: gh/devloop-starter PR #7 (early feedback loop)

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally terse — prefer code and smoke tests over long prose in the starter.
- Please add any friction you hit while trying the flow under the "issues" section of the repo.

Unresolved: should we include a tiny dedicated free-hosted sandbox endpoint for non-local demos? Pros: remove local friction. Cons: operations + cost. Flagging for product ops.
